title: Natural single-source internal Hom-complex comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $P$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $T_P=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(P,-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], assumed additive. Write $P[0]$ for the cochain complex concentrated in degree zero [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. On the category of all integer-indexed cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules there is a natural isomorphism of functors $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[0],-)\cong T_P^\bullet$, where the left side is the sheaf-valued Hom-complex functor [def-pur-hom-complex] and the right side applies $T_P$ termwise. No boundedness, local freeness, or exactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes: product terms, differential, and functoriality in the coefficient complex

proof.text: In degree n project the product Hom(P[0]^p,K^(p+n)) to p=0. All other factors are zero because their source is zero. Insert the identity into the p=0 factor and zero into every other factor for an inverse; verify both identities on all product projections. Zero internal Hom follows sectionwise from uniqueness of a linear map out of zero.

Project the Hom-complex differential formula to p=0. The source differential is zero, so the signed precomposition term vanishes. The remaining term is postcomposition by d_K. Thus the projections and their inverses form chain maps and component chain isomorphisms.

Specialize the Hom-complex map formula to the identity on P[0] and a chain map f:K to L, at p=0. It states that the Hom-complex map followed by projection is projection followed by Hom(P,f^n). Extensionality for chain maps proves naturality. NatIso.ofComponents assembles the isomorphisms; inverse naturality follows from the inverse identities.

theorem homComplex_single_natIso (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u})
    (P : SheafOfModules.{u} (AlgebraicGeometry.moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    [((SheafOfModules.homFunctor X.sheaf).obj (op P)).Additive] :

      (op ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (AlgebraicGeometry.moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj P)) ≅
      ((SheafOfModules.homFunctor X.sheaf).obj (op P)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
